clue.text: Commercial centre with mail being sent out

indicators.note: letters sent out are dispatched in all directions, so these two words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A business hub where the post is being dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being sent out' rearranges the ten letters of CENTRE and MAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mercantile describes trade and merchants, i.e. commerce.

clue.text: You must restrain little kid, not the first or last to give shout of excitement

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: the word for the kid loses its opening and closing letters

parts.note: a nipper is a small child

explanation.surface: A parent must hold back a small child who keeps yelling.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipper is British slang for a small child; 'not the first or last' strips both its ends before 'must restrain' wraps YE round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection: yippee is a cry of delight or glee.

clue.text: Most worn-out stuff Eric's chucked

indicators.note: things chucked are thrown about, so these letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Eric has thrown away his shabbiest belongings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chucked' rearranges STUFF and ERIC'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the scruffiest thing is the shabbiest, most worn and untidy.

clue.text: Noble king who went mad, with head sinking down maximally

indicators.note: the first letter sinks as far as it can go, to the very bottom of this down entry

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king who loses his reason

explanation.surface: A nobleman linked to a mad king whose head droops as low as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head sinking down maximally' sends LEAR's L to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an earl is a rank of the British peerage, a nobleman.

clue.text: Wrong piece of equipment for workshop

definitions.meaning: a wrong here is a sin or moral failing
a clamp fixed to a bench that grips the work

explanation.surface: A tool in the workshop that has been wrongly chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: wickedness, and the gripping clamp (vise in American spelling).

clue.text: To this point one is only an imaginary beast?

parts.note: yet means so far, up to now
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something so far proved to be merely a creature of fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hedges: the creature may yet be real.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a beast whose existence is unproven.

clue.text: Drunk is captured in something of a pantomime act

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters reel into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A drunk is caught on stage during a comic routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' rearranges IS CAPTURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: hurling a creamy dessert into someone's face is a stock slapstick routine in pantomime, the British Christmas stage show.

clue.text: Birds that are little, not grand, rising from stones

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising reads the letters from bottom to top
the letter standing for grand is removed

parts.note: eaglets are young eagles
G is short for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Young birds soaring up from rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not grand' turns EAGLETS into EALETS; 'rising' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: stelae are upright carved slabs or pillars used as monuments.

clue.text: Tramp sleeping rough maybe has collected one set of papers

indicators.note: collecting something takes it in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a dosser is a homeless person, a British slang term
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A homeless man has gathered up a bundle of documents.
explanation.walkthrough: A DOSSER is British slang for a vagrant who dosses, or sleeps rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dossier is a file of documents on a person or subject.

clue.text: Finally you may get left in space flying in this?

definitions.text: Finally you may get left in space flying in this?

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
flying letters are in motion and land in a new order
finally picks only the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An astronaut might end up stranded in space while travelling in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' gives U, which joins L inside 'flying' SPACE, rearranged as CAPSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a space capsule is the small craft that carries astronauts.

clue.text: Learner will soon be leaving primary school to pay attention

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

parts.words: will soon be leaving primary school
parts.note: a child who is ten will soon move on, as British children leave primary school at eleven

explanation.surface: A pupil about to finish junior school told to concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: British primary schools take children up to eleven, so a pupil who IS TEN will soon leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to listen is to heed or attend to what is said.

clue.text: Woman setting about some men nastily

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters run backwards
some takes just part of the following words' letters

explanation.surface: A woman launching a nasty attack on several men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ENNA from 'men nastily'; 'setting about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Anne is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Switch in plane trip to give source of illumination

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: a flight is a journey by air
a switch is a whip, and to lash is to whip

explanation.surface: Flicking a switch on a plane journey to turn on a light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a light switch but means LASH, as with a whip.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flashlight is a torch, a portable lamp.

clue.text: Superstar idol? Time to get into hard world, little fellow!

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

parts.note: the earth is our world
Rob is a shortened form of Robert, a man's name

explanation.surface: A pop idol told it's time to break into a tough world, young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' puts T inside EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a heartthrob is a celebrity who is the object of adoring crushes.

clue.text: Clothes receptacle that's green inside — bit of headgear kept outside it

indicators.note: the headgear surrounds everything else

parts.note: a hat is an item worn on the head

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another

parts.note: a bin is a container
lime is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A clothes bin painted green, with a hat perched on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the green goes inside the receptacle, then the headgear goes around the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic synonym: habiliment means attire or dress.

clue.text: Home food, it's said, is natural

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: spoken, so the word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: bread is a staple food

explanation.surface: Home cooking described as natural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's said' swaps BREAD for BRED, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an inbred quality is innate, inborn rather than learnt.

clue.text: Young rebel defeated prominent LibDem but not Conservative

parts.note: beat means defeated

indicators.note: 'but not' says the politician's name is wanted except for one letter, which is dropped

parts.note: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats, a British political party

explanation.surface: A young protester beat a leading Liberal Democrat but not a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes C from NICK, the first name of Nick Clegg, the Liberal Democrat leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a beatnik was a 1950s bohemian rebelling against convention.

clue.text: City engineers in South Africa and Britain

parts.note: ZA is South Africa's international code

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: GB is Great Britain
RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A city with engineers working in South Africa and Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RE inside ZAGB.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Zagreb is the capital of Croatia.

clue.text: Splatter item of furniture with gold and black

parts.note: a bed is a piece of furniture
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Daubing a bed with gold and black paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bedaub is to smear or plaster with paint or mess.

clue.text: Ardent temp working in part of the firm

indicators.note: letters at work are busy being reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A keen temporary worker busy in one section of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges ARDENT TEMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a department is a division of an organisation.

clue.text: Pieces for one not quite secure?

indicators.note: the word falls just short, its last letter missing

parts.note: solid means firm and secure

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a solo arrangement is a little unsafe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces for one' suggests single fragments; it means musical pieces for one player.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural: soli are musical works or passages for a single performer.

clue.text: Good person with something irritating, a sort of pain

parts.note: ST is short for saint
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A saintly person suffering an annoying ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a stitch is a sharp pain in the side, often from running.

clue.text: Hearing not good? It's awful — a medical condition

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not leaves out the letter that follows

explanation.surface: Poor hearing is dreadful, a real ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G from HEARING, and 'awful' rearranges HEARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hernia is a rupture where an organ pushes through tissue.

clue.text: Ruler from East on edge after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A ruler from the East living on the brink after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' looks political, suiting a ruler; here it only turns the edge word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an emir is a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Very loudly disposed of a strong drink

indicators.note: something disposed of is taken away

parts.note: a stiff drink is a strong one
ff is fortissimo in music

explanation.surface: Someone noisily knocking back a strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed of' removes FF from A STIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine.

clue.text: Unbelief is conveyed in article by those people

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: conveyed in means carried inside

parts.note: them refers to those people

explanation.surface: Godlessness carried in a piece of writing by certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a piece of writing, but it is the grammatical article.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: atheism is disbelief in any god.

clue.text: Permit unknown character to show disapproval? Fine!

parts.note: a ticket is a permit to enter
y is an unknown in algebra
to boo is to jeer

explanation.surface: Letting a stranger jeer, and declaring it all fine.
explanation.walkthrough: TICKETY-BOO is dated British slang for all right.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation: tickety-boo means in good order, everything as it should be.

clue.text: Stick designation of drug on container

indicators.note: on means attached at the end

parts.note: a can is a tin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A cane labelled with a drug's name on its box.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cane is a walking stick or rod.
